title: What is a webhook?
subtitle: A doorbell for your software.
takeaway: A webhook sends a message when an event happens.

boards.heading: Check. Then process.
boards.note: Verify the sender. Handle repeats safely.

turns.speaker: student
turns.text: Pip, my app keeps asking the store if a new order arrived.

turns.speaker: tutor
turns.text: That is polling. Like opening your front door every minute to check for a parcel.

turns.speaker: tutor
turns.text: A webhook is more like a doorbell. When the order happens, the store sends a message.

turns.speaker: student
turns.text: So my app waits for the bell instead of checking all day?

turns.speaker: tutor
turns.text: Exactly. The message goes to an address your app provides.

turns.speaker: student
turns.text: And I trust every person who rings?

turns.speaker: tutor
turns.text: No. Verify the sender. Someone else can knock too.

turns.speaker: student
turns.text: What if the same delivery rings twice?

turns.speaker: tutor
turns.text: Use the event ID to avoid processing it twice. Retries can happen.

turns.speaker: student
turns.text: So an event, a message, then the right action.

turns.speaker: tutor
turns.text: That is the idea. Your software gets a doorbell.

turns.speaker: student
turns.text: Please tell it not to ring during dinner.
